newsitem.title: UK: GKN to appeal U.S. court ruling on Meineke.
newsitem.headline: GKN to appeal U.S. court ruling on Meineke.

text.p: British engineering giant GKN Plc said Friday it would appeal a U.S. court order to pay $601 million in damages for misusing advertising fees paid by its Meineke Discount Mufflers franchisees in the United States.

GKN said it expected to take its case to the U.S. court of appeals in a month or so to appeal against what has been described as one of the biggest awards against a British company in the United States.
"We have been apprised by our lawyers and we think we are on strong grounds," a GKN spokesman told Reuters.
The award, announced late Thursday, includes $591 million in punitive damages and $10 million in interest.

One analyst said the amount of damages was above expectations but was confident it would be scaled down after an appeal. "It will definitely be lower, but what is important is it that now we see some direction," she said.

The U.S. district court's judgment ended four years of litigation involving Meineke, which has been accused of improperly taking millions of dollars for its own use from an advertising fund built up by franchisees.
The jury found last month after a six-week trial that Meineke had committed fraud by taking the money in breach of contracts with its franchisees.
GKN, which reported its 1996 earnings on Thursday, avoided making any provisions for damages.
"We did not because we were not sure how much we should be providing. A range of figures were being speculated," the GKN spokesman said.

The company amended its results overnight by making a provision of 270 million pounds ($435 million) as exceptional charges. Its amended pretax, pre-exceptional profits stood at 92.8 million pounds ($149 million).

"This includes interest and legal costs likely to accrue pending the outcome of the appeal and will be treated as an exceptional charge in the 1996 accounts," GKN said. The company's appeal is expected to take about 18 months to resolve.
The company had expressed fears last month that the damages could top $740 million. GKN has cash reserves of 528 million pounds ($850 million).

U.S. District Court Judge Robert D. Potter tripled the jury's Dec. 18 finding on compensatory damages, which was put at $197 million. The original decision also had awarded another $150 million in punitive damages, now folded into the judge's award of $600.97 million.
